summary: Recent updates to the 2D graphics component of Firefox have focused on improving text rendering efficiency and accuracy. By tightening various processes, such as limiting the number of components assigned during glyph shaping and ensuring that incomplete glyph data is cleared if the shaping process fails, Firefox aims to deliver more reliable rendering of text. Additionally, optimizations were made to the caching of shaped words, employing a modified hash method to enhance performance. These changes not only streamline text processing but also lead to an overall **improvement in how clear and accurate text appears** on the screen, which is essential for user experience in web applications.
